All 22 tests pass and the code compiles cleanly with `gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Werror`. Here's what was implemented in `ringbuf.c`:

- **`rb_create`** / **`rb_destroy`** — allocates/frees an opaque ring buffer with a capacity-checked byte array
- **`rb_write`** — copies data into the buffer, handling wrap-around at the end of storage; returns how many bytes were actually written (clamped to free space)
- **`rb_read`** — removes oldest bytes from the buffer, also handling wrap-around; returns count read
- **`rb_peek`** — non-destructive copy of oldest bytes (uses a temporary head index)
- **`rb_size`** / **`rb_capacity`** — query current fill level and total capacity
- **`rb_clear`** — resets head/tail/count to zero

All functions are NULL-safe per the spec.
